en: Now, the Hymn for Seeking Forgiveness for Offenses against Śiva: First, due to the influence of past karma, You cause me to experience impurity while situated within my mother’s womb; there, the digestive fire intensely boils me amidst the filth of feces and urine. Whatever suffering torments me there beyond measure—how could it possibly be described? O Śiva, Śiva, Śiva! O Blessed Mahādeva, O Śambhu, my offense must be forgiven! 1

In childhood, my body was drenched in filth due to excessive suffering; I had no thirst for drinking mother’s milk, yet creatures born of the qualities of worldly existence tormented me through my senses.
Overpowered by weeping from the pain of various diseases and the like, I did not remember Śaṅkara—forgive me...

(1) Now that I am mature and established in youth, I have been bitten in my vital joints by the five serpents of sensual objects; my discrimination is destroyed, and I am settled in the pleasure of relishing sons, wealth, and young women. (2)

Alas, my heart is devoid of Śiva-consciousness; it is mounted upon pride and arrogance—forgive me... (3) In old age, with the senses failing and the intellect robbed of its movement by the afflictions of fate and the torments of sinful diseases, my body is emaciated, lacking vigor and miserable;
my mind, empty of meditation on Dhūrjaṭi, wanders through false delusions and cravings—forgive me... (4)

O Enemy of the Asuras, it is not possible for me to attend to the Smārta rites—which are known to be crowded with transgressions due to their dense procedural details—nor can I manage the Śrauta rites; how then, O Lord established by the twice-born, shall I proceed on the path of Brahman?

Through inquiry, the Dharma has been understood via hearing and reflection (*śravaṇa* and *manana*), but what remains to be meditated upon (*nididhyāsita*)? ... Having bathed at dawn during the ritual of ablution, I have not brought water from the Ganges; nor have I ever gathered the leaves of the wild bilva tree from the thicket for the purpose of worship.

A garland of lotuses blooming in the lake was not brought for your sake; forgive me. (6) The *liṅga* was never bathed with milk mixed with honey and ghee, nor with curd and sugar; it was never smeared with sandalwood paste and the like, nor worshipped with flowers fashioned of gold.
It was never honored with incense, camphor lamps, various flavorful offerings, or edible delicacies; forgive me... (7)

Having meditated upon that which is called Śiva within the mind, you gave no abundant wealth to the twice-born; no oblation was offered by you into the mouth of the sacrificial fire with seed-mantras numbering in the hundreds of thousands.
You did not perform penance on the banks of the Ganges through vows, recitations, restraints, the chanting of the Rudra-hymns, or the Vedas... [O] you who are patient!

Abiding in the lotus-place, where the breaths are the earrings of the *praṇava*, in the subtle path, in the peaceful internal mind—where the manifest glory has dissolved into the supreme form of light.
O Knower of the Linga, in this discourse on Brahman, I do not remember Śaṅkara, who dwells within the entire body; forgive me...

(9) Salutations to You, the unattached and pure, devoid of the three qualities, who have destroyed the darkness of delusion; with Your gaze fixed upon the tip of the nose, You whose faults are known and who are never seen [by the senses].
In my state of madness, I do not remember You, Śaṅkara, who are free from all stain and impurity; forgive me... (10)

O Śaṅkara, whose crest is illuminated by the moon, who destroys Smara, who bears the Gaṅgā, whose throat and ear-pits are adorned with serpents, in whose eyes the fire of Vaiśvānara blazes, who wears beautiful garments made from the skin of his own tusks, who is the essence of the three worlds, O Hara—for the sake of liberation, direct all the movements of your mind toward Him; what is the use of other ritual acts?
What is the use of this wealth obtained through horses and elephants, or what is the use of a kingdom? What is the use of sons, wife, friends, and cattle, or of the body and the home?
Knowing all this to be momentary, abandon it from afar with your feet; for the sake of your own soul, following the words of the Guru, worship, worship the Beloved of Śrī Pārvatī.
While looking on, life perishes; youth goes to its decay day by day; days that have passed do not return; Time is the devourer of the world.
Fortune is as fickle as the breaking waves of water, and life is as fleeting as lightning; therefore, O Giver of Refuge, protect me now who have come to you for shelter.

Forgive all this—whether committed by hand or foot, born of speech or body, produced by action, or arising from the ears or eyes, whether mental or otherwise, whether prescribed or forbidden. Victory, victory to you, O ocean of compassion, Śrī Mahādeva, Śambhu! (14) Thus [ends the hymn] of the venerable Paramahaṃsa Parivrājaka Ācārya...
The Hymn for Seeking Pardon for Offenses against Śiva, composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda, is complete.
